subject: Bridge of Responsibilities - MOP, Runway & SLA clarifications
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@optimahealth.com>, Evan Ross <evan.ross@optimahealth.com>, Procurement Team <procure@optimahealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Bridge of Responsibilities - MOP, Runway & SLA clarifications

Hi Monica / Tessa —

Quick handoff for OptimaHealth (Deal RDW-2026-OPT-732). We closed last week with the following headline commitments that CS will need visibility on:

- Initial pilot: 50k tokens/day average for first 30 days (expected burst to 120k/day on certain business hours).
- Latency target: p95 <= 350ms for text-generation routes; agreed exception for complex reranking flow (p95 <= 750ms).
- Data residency: US region only; no cross-region fallbacks.
- Acceptance: three acceptance prompts and one integrated test harness run with Optima’s QA (contact: Aisha).

Attached: MutualActionPlan_Optima_v1.xlsx (MOP draft) and SOW_Optima_DRAFT.pdf. Procurement looped — they expect SOW revisions and a brief run-of-show for go-live.

Asks:
1) Please nominate primary CS lead and implementation owner.
2) Confirm whether we can support the burst profile within the Dedicated pool or if we should schedule a warm-up on a dedicated staging instance.
3) Any preflight security evidence needs (Aisha mentioned a quick SOC 2 artifact check).

Internal note: We approved a one-time SLA exception for reranking latency during the 30-day pilot (sales committed this to secure the pilot). If this needs escalation to infra, flag it to Karthik.

Thanks — I assigned tentative owners in the MOP (column: proposed_owner).

Lauren
Lauren Bishop | Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: MutualActionPlan_Optima_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), SOW_Optima_DRAFT.pdf (pdf stub)
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@optimahealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Bridge of Responsibilities - MOP, Runway & SLA clarifications

Thanks Lauren — good summary. A few clarifying questions before I take ownership: 

1) Burst profile: is the 120k/day a predictable hourly window (e.g., 9a–11a ET) or ad hoc? If predictable we can schedule reserved warm nodes.
2) The acceptance tests — does Optima have an existing harness (Jenkins/Playwright) or do they expect Redwood to run integration tests?
3) Security evidence: Aisha, could you share the specific artifacts you need (SOC 2 sections, network map, list of endpoints)?

Tentative assignment: I propose Tessa Morgan as Implementation Lead (primary POC for day-to-day onboarding) and Monica as Program Sponsor for the first 45 days. Karthik — can you confirm we have authorization for a one-time increase to reserved capacity for week-of-go-live if needed?

I'll pull the MOP and add a high-level sprint0 checklist and milestone dates.

-Monica
Monica Patel | Head of Customer Implementation | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | +1 650-555-0199

Subject: Re: Bridge of Responsibilities - MOP, Runway & SLA clarifications

Monica — answers below inline and attached updated MOP with proposed sprint0 calendar.

1) Burst profile: Optima says primary traffic spike is predictable (weekdays 09:00–11:30 ET). We should plan for scheduled warm capacity for those windows rather than ad hoc autoscale.

2) Acceptance harness: Evan confirmed they have a lightweight Jenkins job that executes the three acceptance prompts and posts results to an S3 bucket. They expect Redwood to run the initial harness with them during the joint acceptance window.

3) Security artifacts: Aisha requested the SOC 2 report summary, network diagram, and confirmation of data-at-rest encryption keys. I uploaded an artifact index to Drive (link below).

I attached a revised MOP (MutualActionPlan_Optima_v1.xlsx) with sprint0 dates, owner column filled (Tessa = implementation lead), and explicit acceptance run steps.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Tessa to schedule a 30-minute kickoff with Optima (include Evan + Aisha + Redwood infra rep).
- Monica to publish sprint0 checklist in the project folder and invite all stakeholders.
- Karthik to confirm go/no-go for the one-time reserved warm node capacity for week-of-go-live and confirm cost center.

Attachments: MutualActionPlan_Optima_v1.xlsx (updated)

Lauren

Subject: Re: Bridge of Responsibilities - MOP, Runway & SLA clarifications

Thanks team — I reviewed the MOP and the ask re: one-time reserved capacity. Approve the warm node for week-of-go-live (cost will be tagged to RDW-2026-OPT-732). Infra, please standby for Tessa's scheduling request.

Operational notes and decision log entry (internal):
- SLA exception for reranking latency during pilot is recorded; CS/Infra to monitor via trace alerts and escalate to Platform on threshold breach (>3 incidents/day).
- Data residency constraint (US-only) is firm — do not enable cross-region fallback for this tenant.
- Procurement: please incorporate the revised SOW page 2 (performance appendix) before DocuSign. Lauren / Procurement, share DocuSign link when ready.

Tessa — you are the implementation owner. Please confirm kickoff time and include an infra engineer (suggest: Diego Fernandez or Marcus Lin).

Karthik
